note: Read by snoop-monitor. Each entry tails a tool's output log for `pattern`; a match counts as a signal, and the monitor is the single thing that fires disk-reclaim. Firing is still gated by /etc/disk-reclaim/arm.key (machine must be armed) — nothing wipes until you provision that key. Patterns for argus + spectre were derived from their vendored source; orin + prx-sd are best-effort (see their notes) and should be watched in /var/log/snoop-monitor.log before you arm.
name: _readme
argus
note: eBPF tracer (C). `argus --json` -> service.log (newline JSON). VERIFIED from src/rules.c + argus-server.c: the JSON "type" field uses these exact uppercase tokens for snoop-relevant events; benign EXEC/OPEN/DNS do not match. PRIVESC is intentionally excluded (fires on legit `please`/su).

name: spectre
note: Behavioral HIDS (Python). Writes /var/log/spectre/alerts.log. VERIFIED from spectre/alerts + main.py: high-severity (threat score over threshold) lines are '[ALERT] ...'; noisy per-event lines use '[WARNING]' and are ignored. CORROBORATING + threshold 2 to stay conservative.

name: orin
note: Forensics/integrity (Python). NB: `orin stream` only feeds raw telemetry to SQLite — the rootkit/tamper DETECTIONS come from `orin analyze`, so the launcher runs a collect->analyze loop into service.log. Pattern matches orin's finding labels. BEST-EFFORT: orin's analyze prints severity and label on separate lines, so watch /var/log/snoop-monitor.log and tune before arming. CORROBORATING.
pattern: rootkit|integrity violation|reverse shell|anti-forensic|unauthorized module|kernel module anomal|masquerade

name: prx-sd
note: Antivirus (Rust). OFF-TARGET (finds malware, not examiners) + noisiest. `sd monitor` -> service.log (tracing). Threat levels are clean/suspicious/malicious; pattern matches a malicious verdict or rootkit indicator. BEST-EFFORT: verdict-line format not documented — verify in /var/log/snoop-monitor.log, or leave this one disabled. CORROBORATING + threshold 2.
